items.title: The disturbing reality behind the affordable housing promise
items.description: Governments across Australia are spending billions to boost the number of rentals available to people on low and middle incomes. A Four Corners investigation found many of these homes were unaffordable for those who needed them most, particularly single-income households.

items.title: Australian woman was cunning 'Sharia judge' in Syrian camp, ABC told
items.description: Speaking exclusively to the ABC, a security source who dealt directly with Australian woman Hodan Abby calls her a driving force behind many of a Syrian detention camp's problems.

items.title: Iran hits Arab states after third round of US strikes in days
items.description: The US says its forces are "prepared and positioned" to ensure freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, after Iran declared it closed following another round of American strikes.

items.title: Australians paying 'unjustified' fees to pharmacies, report says
items.description: Taxpayers are missing out on cheaper medicines due to backroom deals by one of Australia's most powerful lobby groups, according to a new report.

items.title: We're back to two competing superpowers and China is pulling ahead
items.description: When it comes to AI, Australia is a spectator at a UFC cage fight between the United States and China, except the spectators are inside the cage with the combatants.

items.title: Sinner triumphs over Zverev for second consecutive Wimbledon win
items.description: The top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev for his second consecutive title at Wimbledon after his German opponent appeared bothered by a knee issue.

items.title: Change to international travel as digital arrival cards roll out
items.description: A digital alternative to incoming passenger cards filled out by everyone entering Australia is to be implemented in the next two years.

items.title: Live: Burke says he will 'not lift a finger' to help suspected ISIS fighters
items.description: The home affairs minister says he will "not lift a finger" to support suspected Australian ISIS fighters held in an Iraqi prison. Follow live.

items.title: As swift parrots kept breeding in this forest, the government realised it had a problem
items.description: It was late 2021 when one of Australia's rarest birds started to arrive in the native forests of Lonnavale. Ecologists had expected it but for a reacting forestry sector, it was "not sustainable".

items.title: Jewish academic fears being met by 'axe or gun' when on campus
items.description: Jewish academics and students say they do not feel safe on campuses, as the antisemitism royal commission prepares to hold a week of hearings scrutinising universities.

items.title: Government to crack down on antisemitism on university campuses
items.description: The new standards will require institutions to adopt definitions of antisemitism, racism against Aboriginal and Torres Straight Islander peoples, and Islamophobia.

items.title: Bangkok pub fire kills at least 27 people
items.description: A huge fire engulfed a pub in Bangkok, killing at least 27 people before firefighters brought the blaze under control.

items.title: Albanese has the Coalition exactly where he wants it
items.description: When the bells resume ringing in the halls of parliament, Anthony Albanese and Angus Taylor will both do well to dispose of any complacency.

items.title: Businesses caught between Labor's trust tax and stamp duty
items.description: Small businesses affected by the change are in limbo as states decide whether to waive stamp duty fees, with industry groups warning relief will be limited unless they sign on.

items.title: Ways to reduce your drinking without quitting altogether
items.description: If you’ve fallen off the Dry July wagon or you just aren’t interested in teetotalling, trying smaller steps to reducing your alcohol intake can still make a difference to your health.

items.title: History quiz: Test your recall on Tay Tay and the Tour de France
items.description: How much do you know about long-past British monarchs, the Salem witch trials and Nintendo games of the 80s? Find out with this week's quiz.

items.title: Every film from Race Around The World week six
items.description: From elephant tracking in Botswana to running up mountains in Nepal, catch up on every week six film from Race Around the World.

items.title: Mate recalls Richard Scolyer's 'magnificent' ride weeks before passing
items.description: As Mark Beretta rode his bike up a steep Tasmanian mountain in March with all his might, it was none other than Richard Scolyer who overtook him.

items.title: Lindsey Graham, pivotal US Republican senator, dies suddenly at 71
items.description: US senator Lindsey Graham, a key Republican who went from a vocal critic of Donald Trump to one of his most loyal allies, has died at age 71.

items.title: Melbourne cafe catches fire three days after alleged drive-by shooting
items.description: Police are treating a fire at an Essendon North cafe as suspicious, just days after the business was sprayed with bullets.

items.title: Family of Perth man raises questions over his Bali death
items.description: The family of Perth man Cameron Hughes, who died in a Bali immigration detention centre, says it has many questions about the circumstances surrounding his death.

items.title: Convicted paedophile to argue multiple-personality evidence unlawful
items.description: A father jailed for abusing two children is appealing against his conviction, arguing evidence given by the multiple personalities of the same witness was unlawful.

items.title: Camp to boost female firefighter participation ditched after one year
items.description: The free camp ran over a weekend in June 2024 for students in years 9 and 10, exploring firefighting activities, road crashes, swiftwater rescues, and physical fitness training.

items.title: 'Like my men's shed': John never left the soccer club he helped create
items.description: For more than 30 years, John O'Toole has quietly helped build a local soccer club. On Sunday, he surpassed his 600th match while playing alongside his sons.

items.title: Illegal camping fine of $345 fine divides coastal community
items.description: A crackdown on illegal camping in Noosa, prompted by hundreds of complaints, has sparked outrage locally, with many arguing fines will not solve the issue.
